standard_clauses.clause_text: Cement shall contain the following percentages by mass: Silicon dioxide (SiO₂) min 17%, Aluminum oxide (Al₂O₃) max 8%, Iron oxide (Fe₂O₃) 3-8%, Calcium oxide (CaO) 60-67%, Magnesium oxide (MgO) max 5%
The residue on 90 micron sieve shall not exceed 10%. Residue on 45 micron sieve shall not exceed 0.5%
Minimum compressive strength at 3 days shall be 16 MPa for 40°C class cement
Yield strength shall be minimum 250 MPa for structural steel bars
Earth resistance shall not exceed 5 ohms for buildings. For equipment earthing, shall not exceed 1 ohm

consumer_faqs.question: What is the ISI Mark and why is it important?
consumer_faqs.answer: The ISI Mark is a quality certification that indicates a product conforms to Indian Standards. It ensures the product meets safety, quality, and performance requirements. ISI Mark is mandatory for certain products like LPG cylinders, cement, and electrical equipment.

consumer_faqs.question: How long does ISI certification take?
consumer_faqs.answer: ISI certification typically takes 45-60 days from application submission. This includes factory audit, sample testing, and approval process. The timeline may vary depending on product complexity and compliance status.

consumer_faqs.question: What is hallmarking and how does it protect consumers?
consumer_faqs.answer: Hallmarking is a mark of purity guarantee on precious metals (gold, silver, platinum). The BIS hallmark ensures the metal meets the claimed purity standard. It protects consumers from fraud and malpractice by independent assay.

consumer_faqs.question: Which testing labs are accredited for steel testing?
consumer_faqs.answer: Multiple accredited laboratories conduct steel testing. The Central Testing Laboratory in Delhi and Regional Testing Centres in major cities are equipped for structural steel testing. Check the BIS website for the complete list of accredited labs in your area.

consumer_faqs.question: How can I apply for ISI Mark certification?
consumer_faqs.answer: Visit the BIS website, fill out the application form with manufacturing details, submit required documents (factory details, quality control plan, technical drawings), pay the application fee, and wait for the audit and testing process.
